strongest_result: When potential-based shaping is applied with changing active coalitions, embedding credits in a fixed population space and recording every transition for every agent restores componentwise telescoping and Nash invariance; if shaping is paid only to active agents, the dropped entry and exit payments reappear as boundary terms that can depend on policy, worked out for two payment conventions.
reason: The invariance theorem is a direct instance of Lu et al. and Devlin and Kudenko applied after zero-padding to a fixed index space, and the boundary diagnosis is a one-line telescoping computation whose exit part is already Grześ's nonzero terminal-potential term. The paper's main value is as a careful typing and accounting critique of one specific method (MARS-RA), not as a general advance. It offers no new algorithm, no learning guarantee and no empirical evidence.

strongest_result: A split-conformal order statistic on room-level Hausdorff wall errors, combined with the 1-Lipschitz property of distance-to-set, gives a marginal finite-sample guarantee with probability at least 1−α that every non-abstained decision of a wall-distance gate matches the decision the reference-wall gate would make.
reason: The main theorem puts together two textbook facts: split-conformal coverage under exchangeability, and the fact that distance to a set changes by at most the Hausdorff distance. Getting a simultaneous guarantee without a union bound follows at once from using one room-level score, and the paper itself says the prior robotics work already establishes this calibrate-then-transfer pattern. It has no empirical calibration, no downstream guarantee beyond the first binary gate, and the time-sharing bound is standard, so it reads as a narrowly scoped technical note with a proposed validation protocol.

strongest_result: A fixed-population, all-transition reward ledger for potential-based shaping under changing active coalitions keeps componentwise telescoping intact, so each agent's payoff shifts by a policy-independent constant. Active-only payment conventions break this, because they drop the entry and exit transition payments and leave boundary terms that can depend on policy (an entry term under both conventions, plus a Grzes-type exit term when the exit transition goes unpaid).
reason: The invariance theorem is the standard telescoping argument of Ng et al., Lu et al. and Devlin-Kudenko, restated in a zero-padded fixed index space. The boundary-term diagnosis is a short calculation that any expert would do in minutes, and the exit term is a direct instance of Grzes's terminal-potential observation. The paper is essentially a careful audit and repair of one specific recent paper (MARS-RA), adds no new technique or general result, and openly lists its own contribution as narrow, so it has little impact beyond that source paper.

strongest_result: A split-conformal order statistic over room-level Hausdorff wall errors gives a radius that, combined with the 1-Lipschitz bound on distance to a set under Hausdorff perturbation, makes every non-abstained decision of a wall-distance gate agree with the reference-wall gate at the same time, with marginal probability at least 1-α.
reason: The result chains two textbook facts: standard split-conformal coverage, and the fact that the distance to a set moves by at most the Hausdorff distance when the set is perturbed. Avoiding a union bound comes directly from scoring at the room level, so an expert would see it immediately. There are no data, no calibration experiment and no downstream guarantee, and the scope is a single threshold in one specific robotics pipeline, so the contribution is a short methodological note with little significance for mechanism design or for multi-agent learning.

strongest_result: Under shared-draw, conditionally independent symmetric single-coin noise with positive reliabilities, a calibrating observer triangle, and edge coverage, cross-observer agreement moments identify observer reliabilities without labels, which in turn identify Bradley–Terry edge probabilities and, on a connected comparison graph, the score vector up to translation.
reason: The main step, recovering single-coin Dawid–Skene reliabilities from a rank-one agreement factorisation via a triangle, is textbook and is credited to Ma et al.; inverting the logit on a connected graph is immediate, so the theorem is a short composition of known facts at the population level only. The paper says itself that it does not deliver incentive compatibility, finite-sample rates, or a working decentralisation of P, and the potential-shaping observation is standard. What remains is mainly a careful diagnosis of how two specific papers relate, which suits a short note rather than a journal contribution.

strongest_result: For bounded, Lipschitz losses, the expected empirical-smoothed CVaR surrogate used in P's zeroth-order method lies uniformly within L_n δ_n + (U_n/α_n)√(2π/s_n) of the true CVaR on the shrunken feasible set. This gives a true-cost gap of at most 2Σb_n, an allocation bound under strong convexity, and a conditional individual-rationality deficit of at most 2b_n.
reason: The main theorem joins known pieces: Wasserstein stability of CVaR, a DKW tail integral (the paper credits this route to Prashanth and Bhat), Jensen's inequality and a standard smoothing bias bound. The welfare and allocation consequences are textbook perturbation arguments. The mechanism-design part is explicitly conditional: mechanism existence, LMI feasibility and the domain-shrinkage error are all left open, so the paper does not advance either the Q or the P line of work in a substantive way.

strongest_result: For bounded, Lipschitz losses, the deterministic expected surrogate (empirical CVaR averaged over batches and smoothed over a ball) stays uniformly within L_n δ_n + (U_n/α_n)√(2π/s_n) of the true CVaR on the shrunken feasible set, which gives a 2B welfare-loss bound, a 2√(B/ρ) allocation bound, and a conditional −2b_n individual-rationality guarantee.

strongest_result: Under shared realised binary comparisons with conditionally independent symmetric observer noise, positive reliabilities, a calibrating observer triangle and full edge coverage, cross-observer agreement moments identify observer reliabilities without labels, and Bradley-Terry inversion on a connected comparison graph then identifies the contribution scores up to translation.

The rest is a first-moment inversion followed by the standard logit edge-difference argument on a connected graph, so any expert would see it immediately. The paper's value is mostly a diagnosis of why the two cited works do not compose and what they leave open. It gives no finite-sample results, no incentive-compatibility mechanism and no experiments, so it reads as a short positioning note rather than a substantive contribution.

strongest_result: If owners can voluntarily migrate divisible work away from a fixed baseline, destination capacities are additive and private migration costs are smooth and strongly convex, then after an electrical-coordinate rescaling the quadratic-payment mechanism of Garjani et al. implements the forecast-conditioned welfare-optimal migration at a unique Nash equilibrium. Individual rationality holds relative to zero migration.
reason: The main theorem only checks that a modelling choice meets the hypotheses of an existing mechanism theorem. The paper itself calls it an application-level specialisation, and it assumes the hard parts: private costs, their curvature and LMI feasibility. The forecast-error certificate is one application of Hölder's inequality, and the regret bound is standard. There is no new mechanism, learning or incentive insight beyond a careful statement of where the two prior papers do and do not apply.

strongest_result: Under assumed smooth, strongly convex private migration costs, voluntary origin-to-destination workload migration with additive residual destination capacities fits the quadratic-payment mechanism of Garjani et al., so that mechanism implements the forecast-conditioned welfare optimum at a unique Nash equilibrium and is individually rational relative to zero migration; a Hölder/dual-norm margin test certifies when the predicted emissions reduction survives NCI forecast error.
reason: The main theorem only checks that a modelling choice satisfies the hypotheses of an existing mechanism theorem, and the paper says so itself.
